messages.subject: Re: [BioGeoBEARS] Error: package ‘ape’ required by ‘BioGeoBEARS’ could not be found
messages.subject_clean: [BioGeoBEARS] Error: package ‘ape’ required by ‘BioGeoBEARS’ could not be found
messages.body_plain:
Hi -- installing APE and other common packages should be very very easy, the fact that it's not indicates that there is some fundamental problem -- bad internet connection/firewall, or maybe the UCLA R-package server is screwy or down.

The most concise intro is to read through the example script, copying and pasting chunk-by-chunk and reading the comments as you go to learn what is happening. The file inputs etc. are discussed there: http://phylo.wikidot.com/biogeobears#script

There is also a recent tutorial that Jeet Sukumaran did at  SSB2015: https://twitter.com/NickJMatzke/status/602228242397929473

Cheers!
Nick

messages.subject: section_the_tree question
messages.body_plain:
I apologize for what is probably a very easy question. I'm trying to run DEC and DEC+j models in BioGeoBears on a dataset that includes time periods (time-stratified) and dispersal multipliers. I have not included an "areas allowed" document, as there is no need.

I am going through an example script and came across the following:
# Divide the tree up by strata (stratified analysis)
#BioGeoBEARS_run_object = section_the_tree(inputs=BioGeoBEARS_run_object, make_master_table=TRUE, plot_pieces=FALSE)

Am I correct in thinking that this is not a command associated with time-stratified settings?

Cheers, Michael

messages.subject: Re: [BioGeoBEARS] section_the_tree question
messages.body_plain:
Hi - no, that *is* associated with time-stratification. So, uncomment it to do time-stratification. That function divides up the tree by time-periods, which is a necessary input... Cheers!
Nick

On Tue, Jun 2, 2015 at 6:01 PM, Michael Forthman <millipede...@gmail.com> wrote:
> I am unable to find any information in the manual about the "resfn" command, and not sure if this is suppose to be a results file or an input file.

resfn = results filename. It's an output, not an input. Just use the default in the script, it's handy later if you want to change the graphics but not re-run the whole ML search from scratch.

cheers, Nick

messages.subject: Stochastic mapping requires single-letter codes
messages.body_plain:
Hi all,

I think I forgot to say this in the stochastic-mapping documentation (such as it is), but: Please note that the stochastic mapping code assumes that all of the areas have single-letter codes — without that assumption, there is no efficient way to store/list ranges of multiple areas.

E.g., "AB" means that 2 areas are occupied, which effects the events that are allowed, etc.

So: *always* use single-letter codes for areas (starting from the geography file), if you ever plan to do stochastic mapping.

(The ML stuff works fine with multi-letter codes -- but, the graphics look better with single-letter codes.)

I will put a check in at some point.

Cheers,
Nick
